configure-first.statement: SAML attributes must be configured in the Admin Console before they can be used as policy rule criteria.

quotes: You must configure SAML attributes to use them when defining policy rule criteria.
you must configure the users' email address SAML attribute in the Zscaler Admin Console.
You can configure SAML attributes using one of the following methods:
import that list into the Zscaler Admin Console
On the SAML Attributes page (Administration > Private Access Authentication > SAML Attributes), you can do the following:
Add new SAML attributes by importing the attributes or adding them manually.

two-methods.statement: SAML attributes are added either by importing a complete list generated from the IdP, or by adding them manually.

quotes: You can import your SAML attributes. This option requires that you generate a complete list of SAML attributes from your IdP, and then import that list into the Zscaler Admin Console.
You can manually add your SAML attributes.

arbitrary-attributes.statement: In Private Access the IdP can provide various authorization attributes to Zscaler Client Connector in the SAML assertion, whereas in Internet & SaaS the assertion is restricted to user identity, group and department attributes.

quotes: In Private Access, various authorization attributes can be provided by the IdP to the Zscaler Client Connector in the SAML assertion, unlike Internet & SaaS, where SAML assertions are restricted to user identity, group, and department attributes.

assertion-each-access.statement: The SAML assertion is used with every application access attempt to ensure that only authenticated users gain access.

quotes: The SAML assertion is used with every application access attempt to ensure that only authenticated users gain access.

no-hosted-user-db.statement: Private Access has no hosted user database for provisioning, so user attributes inside SAML assertions cannot be viewed in the Admin Console: the assertions are encrypted and stored locally by Zscaler Client Connector.

quotes: Private Access does not use a hosted user database for provisioning, so user attributes within SAML assertions cannot be viewed within the Zscaler Admin Console.
SAML assertions which contain these user attributes are encrypted and stored locally by Zscaler Client Connector.

table-fields.statement: Each registered attribute has a Name, which is only a reference and might differ from the SAML Attribute entry; a SAML Attribute, which is the attribute as specified in the IdP; and an IdP Name, the IdP configuration in the Admin Console where it was imported or added.

quotes: This name is only for reference and might not be identical to the corresponding entry in the SAML Attribute column.
The SAML attribute as it is specified in the IdP.
This is the IdP where the attribute was imported or added from.

limit.statement: The Private Access ranges and limitations list 100 SAML attributes under Authentication.

quotes: | SAML Attributes | 100 attributes |

limit.conditions: The row sits under the Authentication heading inside the 'Private Access (ZPA) Ranges and Limitations' part of the unified ranges page; the ZIA part of that page has no SAML attribute row. The ZSDK ranges page repeats the same figure.

auth-service-replaces-page.statement: With a subscription to Authentication Service for users, the SAML Attributes page is replaced by the Session Attributes page: the SAML Attribute column becomes Session Attribute, and the Add SAML Attribute button, the Edit and Delete buttons, and the filter by IdP are hidden.

quotes: The SAML Attributes page is replaced by the Session Attributes page if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
The ability to filter the list to show attributes for a specific IdP is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
The Add SAML Attribute button is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
The Edit button is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
The Delete button is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
then the SAML Attribute column is replaced with the Session Attribute column.

zpa-61-limit.title: Authoritative ZPA SAML attribute limit
zpa-61-limit.resolution: The Private Access ranges and limitations page lists 100 SAML attributes (claim limit).

name-match-exactness.title: Whether the registered SAML Attribute must match the assertion exactly, and whether case matters
name-match-exactness.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "This must match the IdP's assertion exactly for policy evaluation to work" and "check ... case-sensitive in most assertions". The captured page says only that the SAML Attribute is the attribute as specified in the IdP. A lab test would register an attribute whose case differs from the assertion and observe whether a rule on it matches.
name-match-exactness.blocks: saying that a case or spelling mismatch is why a SAML criterion never matches

migration-continuity.title: What happens to SAML criteria in existing rules when a tenant moves to Authentication Service for users
migration-continuity.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "When migrating ... the SAML Attribute objects are converted to Session Attributes. Existing policy rules that reference SAML attributes should continue to work post-migration". The captures say the page and the rule criteria are replaced, not what happens to existing rules. Resolve from the Authentication Service migration documentation or a lab tenant.
migration-continuity.blocks: promising that rules survive the move
